svg.text: FIGURE 5: NETWORK REDUCTION & EQUIVALENCE TRANSFORMATIONS ENGINE
Source Transformations, Wye-Delta (Y-Δ) Dual Conversions, and Balanced / Unbalanced Bridge Analytics

g.text: 1. Source Transformations & Redundancies
Thévenin-Norton Terminal Equivalence
• A real voltage source (V_s in series with R_s) is identically equivalent
to a real current source (I_s in parallel with R_s) AT TERMINALS A-B:
I_s = V_s / R_s ⟺ V_s = I_s · R_s (R_s unchanged!)
Polarity Rule:
Current arrow of I_s MUST POINT TOWARDS the positive terminal of V_s!
• Internal power dissipation is NOT equal! Equivalence is strictly terminal.
Series and Parallel Source Combinations
Voltage Sources in Series:
V_eq = ∑ (± V_k) (Sum aiding, subtract opposing)
Voltage Sources in Parallel:
Allowed IF AND ONLY IF voltages are identical (V₁ = V₂ = V)!
If V₁ ≠ V₂, circulating current I = (V₁ - V₂)/0 → ∞ (Violates KVL!).
Current Sources in Parallel:
I_eq = ∑ (± I_k) (Add aligned, subtract opposing)
Current Sources in Series:
Allowed IF AND ONLY IF currents are identical (I₁ = I₂ = I)!
If I₁ ≠ I₂, violates KCL at the intermediate junction!
Redundant Element Deletion Axioms
Axiom 1: Element in Parallel with Ideal Voltage Source
• Any resistor, inductor, capacitor, or current source in direct PARALLEL
with an ideal voltage source CAN BE REMOVED when analyzing the
rest of the network! Terminal voltage is already clamped at V_s.
★ External circuit currents are 100% unaffected by removing it!
Axiom 2: Element in Series with Ideal Current Source
• Any resistor, inductor, capacitor, or voltage source in direct SERIES
with an ideal current source CAN BE SHORTED / REMOVED when
analyzing the external network! Terminal current is already fixed at I_s.
★ External node voltages are 100% unaffected by removing it!
★ Critical Exception: When Redundant Elements Matter!
Do NOT remove the element if:
1. You are asked to calculate the TOTAL POWER supplied by the source!
The parallel resistor draws current from the voltage source (P = V²/R).
The series resistor develops voltage across the current source (P = I² R).
2. The element controls a DEPENDENT SOURCE somewhere in the circuit!
(e.g., controlling voltage v_x is across that parallel resistor!).
3. If neither applies, prune aggressively to save precious exam time!
2. Delta-Star (Δ - Y) Equivalence
Topology & Node Notation
• Three External Terminals: A, B, C.
• Delta (Δ / Mesh) Resistors: R_ab (between A-B), R_bc (B-C), R_ca (C-A).
• Star (Y / Tee) Resistors: R_a (connected to A), R_b (B), R_c (C), meeting at neutral N.
• Equivalence condition: Resistance measured between any pair of terminals
(with third open) must be identical in both networks!
R_AB(Δ) = R_ab ∥ (R_bc + R_ca) ≡ R_a + R_b = R_AB(Y)
Delta to Star Conversion (Δ → Y)
★ Universal Mnemonic Rule:
R_arm(Y) = (Product of Adjacent Delta Sides) / (Sum of All 3 Delta Sides)
Let Perimeter Sum Σ = R_ab + R_bc + R_ca:
R_a = ( R_ab · R_ca ) / Σ
R_b = ( R_ab · R_bc ) / Σ
R_c = ( R_bc · R_ca ) / Σ
• Symmetrical Delta (R_ab = R_bc = R_ca = R_Δ):
R_Y = R_Δ / 3 (Each Star arm is 1/3 of Delta resistor!)
Star to Delta Conversion (Y → Δ)
★ Universal Mnemonic Rule:
R_side(Δ) = Sum of Connected Arms + (Their Product / Opposite Arm)
Alternatively, let Pair Sum Π = R_a R_b + R_b R_c + R_c R_a:
R_ab = R_a + R_b + ( R_a · R_b ) / R_c = Π / R_c
R_bc = R_b + R_c + ( R_b · R_c ) / R_a = Π / R_a
R_ca = R_c + R_a + ( R_c · R_a ) / R_b = Π / R_b
• Symmetrical Star (R_a = R_b = R_c = R_Y):
R_Δ = 3 · R_Y (Each Delta resistor is 3× Star resistor!)
Dual Element Transforms: Inductors & Capacitors
1. Inductors (Z_L = sL ∝ L):
• Follows EXACTLY identical formulas to resistors:
L_Y = L_Δ / 3 | L_Δ = 3 · L_Y
2. Capacitors (Z_C = 1/(sC) ∝ 1/C):
• Admittance behaves like conductance: Y_C = sC ∝ C!
C_Y = 3 · C_Δ ⟺ C_Δ = C_Y / 3 (INVERSE RELATION!)
Notice: To obtain equal impedance, Star capacitor must be 3× larger!
★ Fatal Exam Trap: Dividing C_Δ by 3 to find C_Y! It MULTIPLIES by 3!
3. Wheatstone Bridge Equilibrium
Bridge Topology & Null Condition
• Four arms: R₁, R₂, R₃, R₄ forming diamond ABCD.
• Supply voltage V_s applied across terminals A and B.
• Detector / Galvanometer R_g connected across terminals C and D.
Null Balance Criterion (V_CD = 0 V):
R₁ · R₄ = R₂ · R₃ ⟺ R₁ / R₃ = R₂ / R₄
★ Opposite Arm Resistance Products MUST BE EQUAL!
Equipotential Properties at Balance
When R₁ R₄ = R₂ R₃, the following conditions hold identically:
• Node Potentials: V_C = V_D (Equipotential Nodes!).
• Detector Current: I_g = 0 A REGARDLESS of detector resistance R_g!
Whether R_g = 0 Ω (shorted) or R_g = ∞ Ω (open), circuit currents are identical!
Total Input Resistance Seen by Source:
R_in = ( R₁ + R₂ ) ∥ ( R₃ + R₄ )
R_in = [ (R₁ + R₂) · (R₃ + R₄) ] / ( R₁ + R₂ + R₃ + R₄ )
• If all 4 arms are identical (R₁ = R₂ = R₃ = R₄ = R):
AC Impedance Bridge Generalization
• For complex impedances Z₁(jω), Z₂(jω), Z₃(jω), Z₄(jω):
Z₁ · Z₄ = Z₂ · Z₃
Requires TWO Independent Real Balance Conditions:
1. Magnitude Balance: |Z₁| · |Z₄| = |Z₂| · |Z₃|
2. Phase Angle Balance: ∠θ₁ + ∠θ₄ = ∠θ₂ + ∠θ₃
• Maxwell Bridge: Measures medium Q inductors against standard C.
• Hay Bridge: Measures high Q (Q > 10) inductors.
• Schering Bridge: Measures unknown capacitance and dielectric loss tan δ.
• Wien Bridge: Measures source frequency f = 1 / (2πRC).
Bridge Sensitivity in Sensor Instrumentation
• Strain gauge sensor: Arm 1 varies as R + ΔR where ΔR ≪ R.
Quarter-Bridge Sensitivity (1 active arm):
V_o / V_s ≈ ΔR / (4 R) (Linearized)
Half-Bridge Push-Pull (2 active arms ±ΔR):
V_o / V_s ≈ ΔR / (2 R) (2× Sensitivity, temperature compensated!)
Full-Bridge Push-Pull (4 active arms):
V_o / V_s ≈ ΔR / R (4× Sensitivity, perfectly linear!)
4. Unbalanced Bridge Thévenin Engine
Thévenin Equivalent Looking into CD Terminals
• When R₁ R₄ ≠ R₂ R₃, detector current I_g ≠ 0 A.
• To solve for detector current I_g, replace the entire bridge with its
Thévenin equivalent network looking into detector terminals C and D:
Step 1: Open-Circuit Voltage V_th = V_C - V_D:
V_C = V_s · [ R₃ / (R₁ + R₃) ] | V_D = V_s · [ R₄ / (R₂ + R₄) ]
V_th = V_s · [ ( R₂ R₃ - R₁ R₄ ) / ( (R₁ + R₃)(R₂ + R₄) ) ]
• Notice: If R₁ R₄ = R₂ R₃, V_th collapses to exactly 0 V!
Step 2: Thévenin Resistance R_th
• Deactivate source V_s (replace ideal voltage source with a SHORT CIRCUIT):
• Terminals A and B become the same electrical node!
• R₁ is in parallel with R₃; R₂ is in parallel with R₄:
R_th = ( R₁ ∥ R₃ ) + ( R₂ ∥ R₄ )
R_th = [ (R₁ R₃) / (R₁ + R₃) ] + [ (R₂ R₄) / (R₂ + R₄) ]
Step 3: Exact Galvanometer Current I_g:
I_g = V_th / ( R_th + R_g )
High-Yield Exam Shortcut: Symmetric Bridge
• Many GATE problems feature symmetric arms: R₁ = R₄ = R and R₂ = R₃ = R'.
Rapid Formulas for Symmetric Unbalance:
• Example Drill (GATE Classic):
Let V_s = 10 V, R = 10 Ω, R' = 30 Ω, R_g = 5 Ω.
Alternative Delta-Star Reduction Method
• If input resistance R_in of unbalanced bridge is required:
1. Convert upper delta (R₁, R₂, R_g) into equivalent star (R_a, R_b, R_c).
2. The resulting circuit has R_b in series with R₃, and R_c in series with R₄.
3. These two series branches are in parallel with each other.
4. Finally, add star resistor R_a in series with that parallel combination.
R_in = R_a + [ (R_b + R₃) ∥ (R_c + R₄) ]
Avoids solving 3 simultaneous mesh equations! Massive exam speedup!
